newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jurors shown bloody crime scene photos.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jurors shown bloody crime scene photos.

text.p: The man who headed the investigation into the killings of O.J. Simpson's ex-wife and a friend testified in Simpson's civil trial on Thursday, taking jurors through the murder scene step by bloody step.

"There was a lot of blood on Ron Goldman's left leg; there was a lot of blood everywhere," former detective Tom Lange said as he pointed to gruesome photographs of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman lying where they died at the hands of a knife-wielding assailant on June 12, 1994.

Simpson, who gained fame as a professional football player, actor and television pitchman, looked away as the photographs were displayed, while Goldman's sister, Kim Goldman, buried her face in her hands.
The morning session was cut short when an alternate juror, a man about 40 who works at a law firm, had to be taken to a hospital suffering from high blood pressure.

Simpson was found not guilty of the murders by a criminal court jury last October but is fighting a wrongful death suit by the families of the victims, who are seeking millions of dollars in compensatory damages for the loss of loved ones.

Attorneys for the plaintiffs had indicated they intended to call Simpson to the witness stand around the middle of November. But lead defence lawyer Robert Baker told Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki on Thursday that Simpson would be unavailable from Nov. 12 to the end of the month while he fights for custody of his and Nicole Brown Simpson's two children, Sydney, 11, and Justin, 9.

Simpson voluntarily gave custody of the children to their maternal grandparents, Lou and Juditha Brown, at the time of his arrest in connection with the murder of their mother. He spent 16 months in jail before and during the criminal trial and sought to regain custody after he was found innocent.
The Browns have resisted his attempts to take the children on a permanent basis. Simpson does have access to them and they frequently spend weekends at his mansion.

The judge in charge of the custody case recenly turned it over to another jurist and Baker said hearings in an Orange County courthouse would take at least two weeks. Simpson spent Tuesday conferring with his custody lawyer and was not in court for his civil trial.

Lange, who retired from the Los Angeles Police Department this year after almost 29 years and now works as a private investigator for criminal defence attorneys, took the jurors through the crime scene with a series of photographs showing the victims, the trail of bloody footprints leading from the bodies and the blood spots spattered over the area.

He said when he arrived at the scene at 4.20 a.m. on June 13 he was met by detectives Ron Phillips and Mark Fuhrman, whom he had never seen before. He also said he saw only one glove at the murder scene.

Simpson's lawyers are trying to prove a police conspiracy centred around Fuhrman, who the defence in the criminal trial branded as a rogue racist cop who planted a bloody glove at the rear of Simpson's mansion in an attempt to frame him.

Fuhrman pleaded no-contest to perjury this month over his denial under oath during the criminal trial that he had used racial slurs. He has since apologised in interviews for lying but has insisted that he did not plant the glove, which matched one found at the crime scene.
